<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/app.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/app.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via AppSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via AppSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AppSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/app.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/app.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 58cb05d7d09d6032abfa27ecf2e47bab6415f297` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `457fcca4a4ef60ba7e612aa4a233217725242b34` — the merge of head `531565de8fad4f0eab038a170f98327ee89025e5` into base `58cb05d7d09d6032abfa27ecf2e47bab6415f297`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 457fcca4a4ef60ba7e612aa4a233217725242b34 && git checkout 457fcca4a4ef60ba7e612aa4a233217725242b34
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 58cb05d7d09d6032abfa27ecf2e47bab6415f297 531565de8fad4f0eab038a170f98327ee89025e5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 58cb05d7d09d6032abfa27ecf2e47bab6415f297 && git merge --no-ff 531565de8fad4f0eab038a170f98327ee89025e5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 58cb05d7d09d6032abfa27ecf2e47bab6415f297
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 58cb05d7d09d6032abfa27ecf2e47bab6415f297` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0ba3d126b55a097fb33a214a4acea35ebc47a756`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts + ui/packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/appDeclaredLanding.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/AppContent.declaredLanding-28450.test.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useNavMemberGates.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx, ui/packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/UnifiedSidebar.tsx, ui/packages/types/src/__tests__/spec-object-refinements-7715.test.ts, ui/packages/types/src/__tests__/imported-defaults-8317.test.ts, ui/packages/types/src/__tests__/app-actions-retired-7469.test.ts, packages/spec/liveness/app.json, packages/qa/dogfood/test/expression-conformance.ledger.ts, .changeset/28450-app-landing-console.md (the prose faces content/docs/** are the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT)

Inputs read: card #28450 body and all six comments (triage 6547078750 / 6548383272, claim 6550280340 and amendments 6550410778 / 6550418134, os-dev-report 6551861740); ruling 6545223246 on #28022 (letter A); PR #28496 body, file list (15 files, +558/−56) and `git diff origin/main...refs/review/pr-28496` at merge base 9b4d1933; the head's check-runs. The cited code was read from the PR head and `main`, never run.

Check-runs on the head at read time: 11 `success` (Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, filter), 7 `skipped` (opt-in and schedule lanes), 24 still `in_progress` (Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Lint ×8 lanes, Type Check ×4 lanes, Test Core 1–8, Live E2E UI). No failure seen; the Type Check and Test Core verdicts were not yet rendered when this record was written.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set narrowing at objectui's `app` node — right, and `!` is right for it.** `AppComponentSchema` (`ui/packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts`) chains the spec's `checkAppLandingItems`, so three documents `main` accepted at objectui's door and `safeValidateSchema` are now refused with the spec's own `custom` issue at the spec's path: `landing.N.item` naming no entry of the app's own `navigation` / `areas[].navigation`; `landing.N.item` naming a `group` / `separator` / `action`; `landing.N.visible` reading `data`. The spec already refused all three (`AppSchema.superRefine(checkAppLandingItems)` at app.zod.ts:2116, pinned in `packages/spec/src/ui/app-landing.test.ts`), so the narrowing closes a mirror gap the objectui#7715 ruling B1 requires closed; the census row in `spec-object-refinements-7715.test.ts` moves the check from `notAttachable` to `attached`, and the census measures the count off `_zod.def.checks`, so the attachment is proven, not listed. `!`, the `**BREAKING**` banner and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` all carry it.
2. **A second public-surface change the diff implies and names nowhere — wrong (should-fix).** `AppComponentSchema` is now a ZodObject carrying a refinement; on zod `^4.6.5` (the `@object-ui/types` dependency) `.extend()` / `.omit()` / `.pick()` on such an object throw at module load. The PR met this itself (`app-actions-retired-7469.test.ts`'s `AppMirror.omit(...)` was rebuilt from `.shape`). In-tree no non-test code derives from `AppComponentSchema` by those methods (`AppSchemaRendererNodeSchema.schema` only wraps it `.optional()`), and neither hotcrm nor the sibling objectui checkout does; but the changeset is the text an upgrading consumer greps and it does not say "derive with `.shape` or `.safeExtend()`". One sentence in `.changeset/28450-app-landing-console.md`.
3. **The console reads `landing` — right.** `AppRootLanding` → `resolveLandingRoute` → `resolveDeclaredLandingRoute` over the trees the member is shown (`navigation` first, then each `areas[].navigation`), each `visible` asked with `gates.evaluateVisibility` with no entry, which is `navEntryVisible(expression, undefined, …)` → `evaluateNavigationVisibility` over the shell evaluator; no match → `findFirstRoute(shownTrees[0])`, exactly today's rule. The predicate roots are `buildExpressionScope`'s and nothing else: `current_user` with `user` / `ctx.user` / `os.user` aliases, and `features`; no `data` (ADR-0068 D1). The root landing (`resolveDeclaredHomePath` → `/apps/:segment`) targets the app root, so it reaches this read point too; there is no second landing resolver that bypasses it.
4. **The fault face — right, and the ruled one.** `evaluateNavigationVisibility` withholds on a fault (objectui#12700), reports it through `reportUnresolvableVisibilityPredicate` with the `withholding` consequence, and the reporter dedupes on `[type, key, source]`, so the double ask (shown trees and once-pending-reads-show trees) and re-renders report each predicate source once. Dogfood row `cel-app-landing` → `enforced` / `fail-soft-log`, enforcement cell naming the evaluator — right; ADR-0137 D4 (a faulting gate is diagnosed, never a silent `true`) is honoured.
5. **Spec prose and liveness — the flip is right; the text is wrong on one point (④ must-fix).** `app.landing` + children `planned` → `live` with `authorWarn` dropped, evidence citing the read point (`appDeclaredLanding.ts#resolveDeclaredLandingRoute`, `AppContent.tsx#AppRootLanding`) — the Spec property liveness check-run is green on it. The describe and JSDoc drop PLANNED. But the describe, as changed, says what is passed over (an entry the reader's gates hide; a faulting `visible`) and the refusal message of `checkAppLandingItems`, unchanged, says a `url` entry "opens something" — while the consumer passes a `url` entry over in silence. See ④.
6. **Pending reads — right.** The landing is resolved twice (shown trees; trees as pending reads would show them) and the root holds on the skeleton while the two disagree; a landing entry binds no `data`, so the predicate answer is identical in both asks and only the target's presence differs — the objectui#13097 invariant holds for a declared landing as it did for the first-item rule.
7. **Order of resolution across trees — right and consistent with the spec.** Spec `collectNavEntriesById` is first-declaration-wins, `navigation` before `areas[]`; the console's `findEntryById` walks `shownTrees` in the same order and `break`s after the first tree that holds the id. A duplicate id across trees resolves the same way at parse and at landing.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28450-app-landing-console.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell: minor`, `@object-ui/types: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: minor`; summary `feat(console)!:`; `**BREAKING**` banner; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: semantic`; one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The `Check Changeset` run on the head is `success`.
- **Level — right.** The kind `semantic` takes at least `minor` on every package the diff moves, and all three are moved: `@objectstack/spec` packs `src/**/*.zod.ts` and `liveness` (its `files`), `@object-ui/types` the mirror, `@object-ui/app-shell` the console. Breaking ships `minor` under the launch-window guard, with `!` and the banner kept.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — right.** No accept set widens; one narrows (objectui's `app` node, judgment ①.1). The arm is BREAKING and the changeset carries the ADR-0087 disposition the registration gate asks of a narrowing arm.
- **`Metadata-protocol: semantic` — right, with the reason stated.** The protocol an author writes against is `@objectstack/spec`, whose accept set for `landing` is byte-identical before and after: no key added, removed or tombstoned, no value newly refused *by the spec*. What changed in meaning is the key itself, from inert (planned) to read. objectui refusing what the spec already refuses is the published-validator narrowing the Clause-② arm declares, not a narrowing of the protocol. The level is `minor` under either kind, so no gate verdict turns on this reading. ⚠️ If the ④ must-fix lands as a spec-side refusal of `url`, the kind becomes `narrowed` and the `@objectstack/spec` entry must then carry its own FROM → TO line (a `url` item → an in-app entry) and the marker text must say so.
- The ADR-0087 marker's reasoning holds for the diff as it stands: an app the spec accepts passes objectui unchanged, so there is nothing for a migration to rewrite.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **A `url` landing item is accepted and passed over — escalated, must-fix (④.1).** Judged against the spec prose as changed: `AppLandingEntrySchema`'s own docblock says an `item` "that opens nothing … is refused at its own path", its `history` says the entry is strict "so a mis-spelled entry is refused, not shipped as an entry that lands nobody", and `checkAppLandingItems`' refusal message names `url` among the entries that open something. The first consumer (`buildItemRoute` answers `''` for `url`; `resolveDeclaredLandingRoute` then `break`s with no report) ships exactly the entry that lands nobody, in silence. The dev classed it `b` and did not file (Prime Directive #10 names a metadata-authoring trap as what gets filed); the spec text edited by this PR does not state it. Answered: wrong as left.
2. **The sidebar does not follow a landing into a second area — escalated, should-fix.** `UnifiedSidebar` elects `activeAreaId` from `visibleAreas[0]` on mount and re-elects only when the visible-area set changes, never from the URL. The spec docblock on `AppLandingEntrySchema` (hits file, unchanged by this PR, implemented by it) says "The landing is a sidebar entry, so the sidebar highlights what the reader landed on" — for an `areas[1+]` target that sentence is not delivered: the right page opens, the sidebar shows area 0. The ruling is about which page opens, and a deep link behaves the same today, so this is not a FAIL; but it is declared-and-not-delivered on the spec's own words and takes a `domain:ui` card (UnifiedSidebar elects the area the current route lives in), not an acceptance note. Answered: escalate to a card.
3. **`features` is bound but not pinned through `AppContent`.** It arrives from the auth config after first render; a landing predicate on it decides on whatever the scope holds when the root renders — the same as a navigation `visible` on `features`, which the sidebar already lives with. Answered: no escalation; the predicate reads the navigation scope by design.
4. **A `doc` landing lands, without the sidebar's doc gate — should-fix (④.2).** Not raised by the dev. `buildItemRoute` does not short-circuit `doc` (only `url` / `action` / `separator` / `group`), and `resolveHref` answers an in-app `…/docs/…` route for it, so a `doc` landing opens the in-app docs portal — consistent with the refusal message, which calls `doc` openable. But `navEntriesShownToMember`'s docblock states "no consumer of this function lands on a `doc`", which this PR makes false, and that function passes no `checkDocTarget` while `UnifiedSidebar` and `nav-menu-renderer` do: a member can be landed on a doc the sidebar hides. Defence in depth only (the server drops an unreadable doc, objectstack#19790), so not a FAIL.
5. Open questions on the card: "Decide and pin which roots the predicate may read" — pinned (`current_user` + aliases, `features`; no `data`), in the spec JSDoc, the liveness note, the dogfood cell, `appDeclaredLanding.ts` and the 12-test pin. Answered. The one-PR cross-domain exception (triage 6547078750) is used exactly as granted: liveness row and dogfood row, plus the seat amendments' prose. The `Skills-docs:` line is present and true (no `skills/**` file teaches `app.landing`).

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts`, against ruling 6545223246 letter A and its first consumer `AppRootLanding` / `resolveDeclaredLandingRoute`:

- Holds against the ruling: the entries are asked in order, the first whose `visible` holds names the landing, no match keeps the first navigation item by `order`. Pinned on both ends (`app-landing.test.ts` for parse; `AppContent.declaredLanding-28450.test.tsx` for the redirect, through the real `AppContent`, `ExpressionProvider` and `MePermissionsProvider`, with the dev's ablations reported 10/12 and 3/41 red).
- Holds against the consumer on every claim the changed describe makes: hidden-by-gates passed over (shown trees); faulting `visible` passed over and reported once (withholding + dedupe); roots `current_user` / `features`, no `data`; `areas[].navigation` and group depth reachable; first-wins order identical at parse and at landing.
- **Must-fix ④.1 — the hits file contradicts its first consumer on `url`, on the exact failure the key was designed to refuse.** After this PR the published spec says, in `checkAppLandingItems`' message, that a `url` entry opens something; in `AppLandingEntrySchema`'s docblock that an entry opening nothing is refused and that no entry "lands nobody" ships; and in the changed describe that only a hidden or faulting entry is passed over. The console passes a `url` entry over with no report. An author who writes `landing: [{ item: 'nav_external', visible: 'true' }]` passes the spec, passes objectui, and every reader opens on the first navigation item with nothing said — silent-inert metadata (ADR-0078), the `homePageId` silent-fallback the docblock condemns, and declared ≠ delivered (Prime Directive #10). Fix at the producer (Prime Directive #12): add `url` to `LANDING_TARGET_REFUSED_TYPES`, drop "or url" from the message, add the `url` case to `app-landing.test.ts` and the apps.mdx refused list, and state the spec-side narrowing in the changeset (②). The console's pass-over then becomes unreachable for a parsed app and stays as defence. (Making the console open a `url` landing is not an alternative: the app root's redirect is an in-app `Navigate`, and "the app opens on an external URL" is not a landing.)
- **Should-fix ④.2 — `doc` landing and the doc gate** (③.4): either pass the sidebar's `checkDocTarget` into the landing's shown trees, or correct `navEntriesShownToMember`'s docblock and say in the spec JSDoc that a `doc` landing opens the in-app docs portal under the server's audience gate.
- **Should-fix ④.3 — the changeset names the refined-mirror consequence** (①.2): one line that `AppComponentSchema` now carries a refinement, so derive with `.shape` or `.safeExtend()`.
- **Should-fix ④.4 — file the sidebar-area card** (③.2) and link it from the acceptance note.
- `ui/packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts` (cited, read): the attachment is the right site — `landing` flows by reference through `SpecAppFields` (not in `APP_SPEC_EXCLUDED`), and this node's own `navigation` / `areas` carry the `id` / `type` the check reads; the 8317 import-boundary list and the 7715 census both account for it. No finding.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/appDeclaredLanding.ts` / `AppContent.tsx` (cited, read): `resolveLandingRoute` keeps the seam, `findFirstRoute` is unchanged, the two-ask pending invariant is preserved. No finding beyond ④.1 / ④.2.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-n3x42r`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibw2uhdSeHYfnZdAf4V`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `65522b14a47ad98a5f173c00d57fe63c35aafc12`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.app-landing-url-item-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/app-landing.test.ts, ui/packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/appDeclaredLanding.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/AppContent.declaredLanding-28450.test.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useNavMemberGates.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx, ui/packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/UnifiedSidebar.tsx, ui/packages/types/src/__tests__/spec-object-refinements-7715.test.ts, ui/packages/types/src/__tests__/imported-defaults-8317.test.ts, ui/packages/types/src/__tests__/app-actions-retired-7469.test.ts, packages/spec/liveness/app.json, packages/qa/dogfood/test/expression-conformance.ledger.ts, .changeset/28450-app-landing-console.md, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (the prose faces content/docs/** are the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT)

Second record on this PR, after FAIL record 6551992138 on head `0ba3d126`. Inputs read: card #28450 body and all eight comments, now including claim amendments 3 (6551999260) and 4 (6552162223); ruling 6545223246 on #28022 (letter A); card #28497 (filed from ④.4); PR #28496 body as rewritten, file list (18 files, +623/−70), `git diff origin/main...refs/review/pr-28496`, and `git diff 0ba3d126 65522b14` restricted to the PR's own files (no `main` commit between the two heads touched any of them, so that diff is the PR's own); the head's check-runs. The three new commits are d4500482 (the `url` refusal), 910aded5 (the `doc` docblocks) and 65522b14 (the migration entry). Judgments ①.1, ①.3, ①.4, ①.6, ①.7 and the pass-over / fault / roots / pending-read findings of the earlier record are re-affirmed unchanged on this head — `AppContent.tsx`, `appDeclaredLanding.ts` (docblock only), the mirror, the three types tests and the console test are byte-identical to `0ba3d126` apart from the docblocks named below — and are not restated.

Check-runs on the head at read time: 11 `success` (Auto Label, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards ×2, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, filter), 9 `skipped` (opt-in and schedule lanes), 26 still `in_progress`: Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, **Check Changeset ×2**, Lint ×8 lanes, Type Check ×4 lanes, Test Core 1–8, Live E2E UI. No failure seen. ⚠️ The two gates this re-review turns on — the changeset level/kind gate and `check-adr-0087-registration` (both under Check Changeset / Lint), and `check:spec-changes` / `check:upgrade-guide` (Type Check) — had not concluded when this record was written; the PR body reports them green locally, which this record does not rely on. Every check must be green before the seat lands.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **New accept-set narrowing in `@objectstack/spec` — right, and declared right.** `LANDING_TARGET_REFUSED_TYPES` is now `group`, `separator`, `action`, `url` (app.zod.ts:1660), so `checkAppLandingItems` refuses `landing[N].item` naming a `type: 'url'` navigation entry at `landing.N.item`, on `AppSchema` and, by the chained refinement, on objectui's `AppComponentSchema` and the `objectui validate` door. What `main` accepted and this head refuses: exactly that one document shape. The refusal message drops `url` from the openable list (now "an object, page, dashboard, report, component or doc entry"), the `openable` suggestion list excludes `url` ids, the `item` describe and the `landing` describe say `url` is refused, the `AppLandingEntrySchema` docblock says "opens nothing inside the app (a `group`, a `separator`, an `action`, a `url`)". `app-landing.test.ts` adds `nav_help_site` to `NAV`, a `url` row to the refused-type table and asserts the dangling-item message does not offer the `url` id; the dev's ablation (`'url'` removed) reports 2/15 red. This is the fix my ④.1 asked for, at the producer (Prime Directive #12), and the console's `routeOf === ''` pass-over is now defence only for a parsed app, as `appDeclaredLanding.ts`'s docblock now says.
2. **The migration entry — a new public surface of `@objectstack/spec`, right.** `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.app-landing-url-item-refused.ts` registers one `SemanticMigration` (`id: 'app-landing-url-item-refused'`) that `gen:migration-registry` concatenates into `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[18].semantic` (gitignored `registry.ts`, generated at install/build/test), from where `os migrate meta` lists it as a TODO on the 17 → 18 hop for every upgrader, and `check:spec-changes` / `check:upgrade-guide` project it in memory.
